items.title: A quasi-coherent module is locally associated to a module on a neighbourhood of any point with quasi-compact neighbourhoods
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file modules.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that a quasi-coherent module on a ringed space is locally, around a point with a fundamental system of quasi-compact neighbourhoods, the module associated to a module over the ring of sections of that neighbourhood (author lemma at source lines 1463-1473, label lemma-quasi-coherent-module). The proof (source lines 1475-1530) isolates the real difficulty, namely that a map between direct sums need not be given by a matrix over the ring of sections, and resolves it by passing to a quasi-compact neighbourhood on which the sections of the direct sums become finite sums, after which the map is a matrix and the resulting associated module has the same presentation as the given one (proof lines 1492-1529). The reduction of the presentation to a matrix over a quasi-compact neighbourhood is the content. H3.
